label: U2 — Apple U1 UWB SiP, EXPOSED LAND PATTERN (module removed)

input.what_it_shows: Five AirTag boards on a bench. The CENTRE board is a component-side board with several packages PULLED OFF, so land patterns that are covered by a package in every other photograph in this project are bare. O'Flynn: 'I pulled some of the chips off to investiate any connections between the test points and the chips.'
input.tool: tools/b_padcount.py, 9/9 selftest, every control watched firing

what_was_attempted: The pad count, the lattice shape and the extent of the Apple U1 module's land pattern.

the_answer_that_was_refused.why_it_looked_right: It passed every reconciliation gate the tool has: nearest-neighbour spacing coefficient of variation inside tolerance, pads sitting on the fitted lattice, and 96% lattice occupancy. A land pattern with three depopulated cells is exactly what a real SiP footprint looks like.

why_it_was_refused.test: --sweep: re-run across 4 box paddings x 5 threshold offsets = 20 combinations, and see whether the answer is a property of the BOARD or of the SEARCH (E07 family 11)
why_it_was_refused.conclusion: NINE different lattice shapes over twenty parameter combinations. Not the count, not the extent, not even the scale-free aspect ratio survives. Nothing quantitative can be taken from this land pattern.

the_physical_reason.statement: The array is roughly 47 x 71 source pixels. At a ~5.7 px lattice pitch with ~3 px pads in a JPEG, individual pads merge and split as the threshold moves. This is a resolution floor, not a method defect: no threshold choice recovers information the photograph does not contain.

what_would_settle_it: A higher-resolution photograph of a depopulated AirTag component-side board. It does not exist in the public record available here: O'Flynn's repository was enumerated on 2026-09-05 and contains exactly eight files in images/ (airtag-tests.jpeg, backside-1000px, backside-fullres, frontside-1000px, frontside-26mm-cropped, frontside-fullres, frontside-tpnames.jpg, frontside-tpnames.psd), all seven images of which this project already holds. airtag-tests.jpeg is the ONLY one showing a depopulated board, and it is the low-resolution one.
what_IS_established_and_is_new: A depopulated component-side AirTag board exists in this project's own image set and had never been used. Land patterns for the removed packages are bare in it.

The Apple U1 module's land pattern is a dense regular rectangular array occupying roughly a fifth of the board's radial width — visibly far larger and far denser than any other footprint on the board. Qualitative, and stated as qualitative.
Two further exposed land patterns are visible on the same board (one near the crystals, one lower-left) and have not been examined.
